label: Confirmed Deaths
source: Government/Defensoría del Pueblo tallies (as of Jul 9, 2026)
contestNote: Union and independent sources dispute how many deaths are directly attributable to blockade-caused hospital shortages (~14 of the total) versus other causes.

label: State of Emergency
deltaNote: Due to expire around Sep 18, 2026 (90 days from the Jun 20 declaration); cocalero federations aligned with Evo Morales have staged an armed vigil ahead of the expiry.

label: Active Blockades
value: San Pablo lifted (provisional); other points unconfirmed
deltaNote: San Pablo bridge blockade (Beni) was cleared by police/military the afternoon of Aug 27, reopened by producers that night, then lifted again early Aug 30 after Marbán producers reached a provisional deal with the government (Defense Minister Justiniano, Beni Governor Egüez): 30,000L of diesel delivered immediately, a pledge of 70,000L total, and a ~72-hour/Friday check-in on compliance — Decree 5676 itself is unrepealed. Status of the Nueva Jerusalén and Ascensión de Guarayos blockade points (active as of Aug 28) is unconfirmed as of this update. Separately, the Pro Santa Cruz Civic Committee's Sun Aug 30 deadline to repeal the decree passed with the government refusing; the committee's extended board meets Mon Aug 31 to decide whether to convene an Asamblea de la Cruceñidad.

label: USD Exchange Rate (floated)
source: Central Bank of Bolivia (official TCO, Aug 29, 2026)
deltaNote: Up from the 15-year peg of Bs. 6.96 before the Jun 29 float. After a late-July peak near Bs. 12.13, the official rate eased to ~Bs. 11.50-11.71 in mid-to-late August before ticking back up to Bs. 11.83-11.93 by Aug 28-29, with peer-to-peer platforms near Bs. 12.05.

label: Inflation (y/y)
contestNote: The IMF forecasts full-year 2026 inflation near 20.7%, but Bolivia's statistics institute (INE) reported an official year-on-year print of just 4.93% for July 2026 — pass-through from the June currency float and December fuel-subsidy cuts had not yet fully hit consumer prices.

label: Diesel Price — Large Consumers (GRACOS)
deltaNote: Up from the prior Bs. 9.80-9.90/L rate; the subsidized Bs. 9.80/L price is unchanged for transport operators and individual consumers
contestNote: Facing backlash over the 84% hike, Deputy Hydrocarbons Minister Hernán Paredes said Aug 25 the decree "has to be modified" toward a more competitive price. But Minister of the Presidency Fernando Aramayo rejected repeal on Aug 27, attributing the decree to IMF conditionality; new blockades against it began Aug 26 in Beni and Oruro. New Economy Minister Christian Morales Burgos, sworn in Aug 25 replacing interim minister Óscar Mario Justiniano, said Aug 26 the decree needs adjustments "to minimize risks" from producer mobilizations; the Pro Santa Cruz Civic Committee set a 72-hour ultimatum (deadline Sun Aug 30) to repeal it before escalating to a region-wide Asamblea de la Cruceñidad.

label: Arrests (crisis-related)
contestNote: MAS-aligned and union groups characterize a portion of arrests and the Evo Morales warrant as politically motivated prosecution.

label: Cerimedo-Linked Detentions
value: 4 held; Cerimedo now under 2 preventive detention orders
deltaNote: Judge Douglas Borda ordered a second six-month preventive detention against Cerimedo on Aug 29, this time for illicit enrichment, to be served at Chonchocoro prison in addition to his existing Palmasola detention over the attempted-femicide case. Cerimedo clashed with Vice President Edmand Lara, who took part in the hearing to request his transfer, calling Lara a "mythomaniac."
